name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program - Pakistan (Master's and PhD degree grants)
provider: U.S. Department of State Fulbright Program, administered in Pakistan by USEFP (United States Educational Foundation in Pakistan)
degree_levels: Master's (needs a four-year Bachelor's, or Bachelor's + Master's, 'totalling 16 years of formal education') and PhD (needs 'a Master's, M.Phil or comparable degree (a minimum of 18 years of formal education)'); applicants may apply for only one degree
covers: USEFP 2027 announcement: 'tuition, required textbooks, airfare, a modest living stipend, and health insurance'. Degree page: awards 'are always contingent upon USEFP budget allocation for the relevant program year.'
eligible_nationalities: Pakistani citizens 'residing (throughout the process) in Pakistan and committed to returning and serving Pakistan' (USEFP degree page)
field_restriction: 'All academic disciplines are eligible, except clinical medicine.' Priority fields named in the 2027 announcement: the sciences, technology and AI, trade and economics, and natural resource management.
work_experience_required: Master's: not required ('Recent graduates are encouraged to apply'), except MBA and Public Policy/Administration applicants, who need 2 years of work experience in the relevant field. PhD: Pakistan-based teaching, research or public-sector experience is 'highly desirable but not required'.
english_test_requirement: GRE General 'is required for all applicants'. USEFP FAQ: 'a minimum score of 145 is required on each section of the GRE', with a higher score on the section most relevant to the field; the 2025 and 2026 announcements state a minimum of 145 Verbal and 145 Quantitative. TOEFL 'is not mandatory with the application, only the selected candidates will be required to take' it (FAQ); older USEFP notices named the Duolingo English Test for shortlisted candidates. IELTS is not mentioned.
next_deadline: The 2027 round's deadline was 2026-04-01 and it is now closed. The 2028 round had not been announced as of 2026-10-11. The 2027 round was posted in a Jan 2026 USEFP newsletter with an April 1 deadline, and a USEFP press release dated 2026-02-20 reported applications open.
cycle: 2027 program (2027-28 academic year) is closed; the next would be the 2028 program
fit_for_applicant: She is eligible for the Master's track only: her 4-year BS gives 16 years of education, the PhD track needs 18, and nutrition/public health is allowed because only clinical medicine is excluded. Blocker: the 2027 round closed 2026-04-01, so Fulbright cannot fund Spring or Fall 2027 entry; the earliest option is the 2028 round for a Fall 2028 start, which needs a GRE of 145+ in Verbal and Quantitative and residence in Pakistan throughout the process, so it conflicts with starting a US program in 2027.
confidence_notes: These facts are from WebSearch text of official USEFP pages; WebFetch was unavailable. The USEFP application portal reads 'applications for 2027 edition are now closed', while some third-party articles (Tribune, Daily Times) still describe the April 2026 round as open because they are stale. The FAQ says USEFP 'hopes to award 100 Fulbright scholarships in 2027' and that a US degree earned within the past 5 years makes an applicant ineligible. A USEFP press release dated 2026-07-17 (per search summary) reports 85 Pakistani master's/PhD awards. In April 2025, during a State Department review of exchange programs, USEFP publicly denied rumours that Fulbright Pakistan was being terminated (Dawn), so future funding levels are somewhat uncertain. Not verified: whether applicants need US admission before applying (the placement process was not checked), the GRE and English-test rules for the 2028 round, and the 2028 dates. Do not confuse with two other programs: the October 2026 'Fulbright 2027' headlines in Pakistani media are about the Fulbright Scholar Program for PhD holders (separate record), and the 2026-10-06 deadline belongs to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program for US citizens.

name: AAUW International Fellowships (Master's and Doctorate)
degree_levels: First master's degree, or an academic or professional doctorate, in a STEM discipline; full-time study at a US-accredited institution. For 2027-28 the program must begin on or before 2027-09-15 and end on or after 2028-04-30.
covers: Current page: a stipend of '$20,000 for a master's degree and $25,000 for a doctorate degree', paid in two installments (at the start and midpoint of the fellowship term). Fellowships are 'one-time awards and are not renewable'. AAUW pages allow the funds for tuition, living expenses and dependent childcare. This is partial funding, not a full scholarship.
eligible_nationalities: Non-US citizens who do not hold US permanent residency and have not applied for a green card (no country list)
gender_restriction: Women (an AAUW fellowship for women; the application criteria refer to the fellow's intent to return to 'her home country')
field_restriction: STEM only: 'The degree must be in one of the STEM disciplines.' 'Nutrition Science' is listed under Life & Biological Sciences. 'Public Health' appears under Health & Medical Sciences (STEM-based) for quantitative/scientific tracks only, and Epidemiology is listed. Eligibility depends on how the degree program is classified, not on the applicant's individual research topic.
work_experience_required: None stated in search results (Not verified)
english_test_requirement: Proof of English via a native-English statement, an English-medium secondary or undergraduate institution, or one semester of full-time study at an English-speaking institution; otherwise a test score, e.g. IELTS 6.5, Cambridge 176 or Duolingo 120 (current page). An older AAUW page accepted only the TOEFL, but the current page supersedes it.
next_deadline: The 2027-28 window ran from 2026-08-17 9:00am ET to 2026-09-17 5:00pm ET and is closed. 2028-29 dates are not yet posted.
fit_for_applicant: On paper she is a strong match: Nutrition Science is a listed STEM field, her 3.85 CGPA clears the 3.5 minimum, and IELTS 6.5 meets the listed score. Blockers: the 2027-28 window closed 2026-09-17, applicants must already be admitted or enrolled, and the award ($20k MS, $25k PhD) is partial; the realistic use is the next (2028-29) cycle once she is admitted or enrolled, if AAUW repeats a similar schedule (not yet posted).
confidence_notes: The dates, amounts, STEM field list, 3.5 GPA minimum, admission requirement ('You must be admitted to or currently enrolled in at least one academic program at the time of application') and English rules are from WebSearch text of the official AAUW page, which a search summary described as updated about 8 days before 2026-10-11. Older AAUW pages (an Aug 1-Nov 15 window, amounts of $18k/$20k/$30k, a TOEFL-only rule) are superseded. On returning home, an older application page lists intent 'to return to her home country to pursue a professional career' as a requirement, and the current page scores 'Fellow's position on return to home country' as a selection factor. Whether a specific nutrition MS/PhD counts as STEM depends on the program's classification and should be checked per program. Not captured: the TOEFL minimum on the current page and any work-experience rule. Other AAUW programs seen in results: Selected Professions Fellowship (2027-28 window 2027-01-05 to 2027-02-18; eligibility not checked) and American Doctoral Fellowship (closed 2026-09-30; described as for US citizens/permanent residents).

name: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS)
provider: P.E.O. International (P.E.O. Sisterhood), International Peace Scholarship Fund
degree_levels: Graduate (advanced) degrees at an accredited US or Canadian institution. Applicants need at least one full year of formal coursework remaining and must be enrolled and in residence in the US or Canada for the entire school year. Doctoral students doing dissertation work only are not eligible as first-time applicants.
covers: IPS policies (per search text): maximum award of $12,500, based on demonstrated need and not intended to cover all academic or personal expenses. Partial funding only.
eligible_nationalities: Women from countries other than the US and Canada; US or Canadian citizens and permanent residents are not eligible ('A student with residency for tax purposes only is permitted')
field_restriction: None stated in search results (Not verified). Online courses, research or internships are not funded unless combined with formal coursework.
work_experience_required: None stated in search results (Not verified)
next_deadline: 2026-12-15 is the last day to submit the Eligibility Form (accepted from 2026-09-15). The completed application is due 2027-02-01 for applicants already enrolled in their graduate program, or 2027-03-15 for applicants not yet enrolled.
cycle: 2027-28 term of study (awards notified May 2027; recipients accept by 2027-06-01)
fit_for_applicant: This is the most realistic external award for 2027 entry, and it is open now: she can submit the Eligibility Form by 2026-12-15, then the full application by 2027-03-15 (or by 2027-02-01 if she has already enrolled for Spring 2027). Blockers: the application must include a confirmation of admission naming the graduate degree program, the award is need-based and partial (maximum $12,500, so it can top up an assistantship but not replace one), and she must sign a promise to return home after the degree or OPT.
confidence_notes: The 2027-28 dates are from the official 'IPS Application Calendar Dates for the 2027-2028 Term of Study' page and PDF (search text). The eligibility, admission-letter ('a copy of the applicant's confirmation of admission' that specifies the graduate degree program; otherwise the application is not considered), return-home pledge and $12,500-maximum rules come from IPS policy and general-information PDFs dated 10/2024 and could change, so they should be confirmed on the live eligibility page. Funds are limited, so not every eligible applicant receives an award. Not verified: any English-test requirement, any field restriction, whether the admission letter is needed at the Eligibility Form stage or only with the full application, and whether a Spring 2027 entrant counts as 'already enrolled' for the 2027-02-01 deadline.
